problem: The wait instruction JNB TI, TX jumps back to the label TX, which sits on MOV SBUF, A. Until TI sets, the loop re-executes MOV SBUF, A again and again, overwriting the transmit register with the same byte. The frame can be corrupted and the listing does not show the intended 'write once, then wait' behaviour. (The RX routine is fine, because there the label is on the JNB instruction itself.)
fix: Put the wait label on the JNB instruction: TX: MOV SBUF, A / WAIT: JNB TI, WAIT / CLR TI / RET. Then SBUF is written once and the CPU spins only on the flag, matching the C version given later.

problem: The last sentence says 'The SMOD divide-by-2 halves the overflow rate seen by the UART, which corrects the factor.' This is the wrong direction: SMOD = 1 makes the UART divide by 16 instead of 32, so it doubles the baud rate. Halving the rate would give 1200 baud, not the 2400 bit/s the answer computes, and it contradicts Section 2 ('Setting SMOD = 1 doubles the baud rate').
fix: Replace with: 'With SMOD = 1 the UART divides by 16 instead of 32, so the baud rate doubles. With SMOD = 0 the same TH1 would give 1200 bit/s.'

problem: 'Hardware sets TI when the stop bit has left' is slightly off. In mode 1 the UART sets TI at the start of the stop bit, not after it has been shifted out completely.
fix: Write: 'Hardware sets TI when it puts the stop bit on the line.'

problem: The closing reason 'because 12 MHz is not a whole multiple of the standard rates' is misleading: 12 MHz is an exact multiple of 2400 (5000 times). The rounding error comes from the fixed dividers, because 12,000,000 / (12 × 32 × 2400) is not a whole number.
fix: Write: 'because 12,000,000 / (12 × 32 × 2400) = 13.02 is not a whole number, so the reload value has to be rounded.'
